To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
diamide at 1 mM decreases by 50% the content of the membrane SH groups of proteins, resulting in enhanced vesicularization of erythrocyts upon metabolic exhaustion.

diamide, a thiol oxidizing agent, decreases the content of SH-groups of erythrocytic membrane proteins, resulting in enhanced vesicular of erythrocyts and changes in the structural state of membrane proteins.

diamide, an SH-oxidizing compound, does not directly interact lipid bilayer of the erythrocyte plasma membranes, but changes the structural state and the microviscosity in the membrane lipid bilayers by disrupting protein-lipoprotein interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a study of the effect of diamide at a low concentration on the physico-chemical state of the main membrane components, which may be of importance in elucidating the role of SH-groups in maintaining the structure and function of erythrocytic membranes.
the effect of SH-oxidizing agents on erythrocyte metabolism and the state of the membrane.
the effect of diamide, a sulfhydryl-oxidizing agent, on the physico-chemical state of proteins of the erythrocyte plasma membrane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of diamide is due to its action upon the SH-groups of the main integral membrane protein, the band 2 protein.

diamide does not affect the lipid bilayer directly but does produce changes in the physi-chemical state of the membrane lipids by disrupting protein-lipoprotein interactions that take place in the membrane as a result of oxidation of the SH- groups and crosslinking of the membrane proteins.

diamide at low concentrations (1 mM) does not directly affect the lipid bilayer but rather changes the physicochemical properties of lipophilic membrane components by disrupting protein-ligand interactions that take place after oxidation of the SH-group and cross-linking membrane proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
diamide, in the concentration range of 1-10 microM, does not induce lipid peroxidation, but produces changes in the structural state of proteins and the lipid bilayer.

diamide, a SH-oxidizing compound, produces changes in the structure of the main integral membrane protein, band 3 protein, and the physicochemical properties of the lipid bilayer, but it does not induce lipid peroxidation in human erythrocytes.
diamide is a useful tool for investigating the role of the SH-groups in the functioning of membrane proteins and in the regulation of the physicochemical properties of lipophilic membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
diamide-induced oxidation of SH-groups of membrane protein leads to changes in the physiochemical properties of membrane lipids, which can be a factor in the pathogenesis of oxidative stress.

diamide-induced oxidation of the SH-group of the band 3 membrane protein leads to changes in its conformation, which in turn affects the structural organization of membrane proteins and the physicochemical properties of membrane lipids.
diamide at the concentration of 1-3 mM is a powerful agent for studying the role of membrane proteins in the regulation of the functional properties of erythrocytic membranes.
